text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today as oil prices spiked on escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, sending U.S. crude up sharply and pushing Brent crude toward $110 per barrel. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher oil prices directly translate to higher revenue and profits — the company benefits immediately when the commodity it extracts becomes more valuable.

The two-week rally (up 15.6%) reflects a broader shift in oil markets driven by supply concerns and tightening. Beyond the Iran attacks, tanker rates have surged significantly, adding roughly $38 per barrel to the true delivered cost of physical oil; this supply-chain friction, combined with production threats to critical chokepoints like Hormuz, has pushed the real cost of oil well above the headline price, supporting higher valuations for producers across the sector.
